source.title: Understanding and Accelerating Neural Architecture Search With Training-Free and Theory-Grounded Metrics
source.authors: Wu-Yang Chen; Xinyu Gong; Junru Wu; Yun-Chao Wei; Humphrey Shi; Zhicheng Yan; Yi Yang; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates training-free architecture metrics against training and test accuracy, but does not test any listed claim version, including the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The reported correlations are about architecture metrics and accuracy across NAS-Bench-201; they do not measure the training–test gap or test a listed version. No rows for cited prior-work results.
record.test_reason: The study tests training-free architecture indicators and NAS performance, not any listed claim version. Its NTK conditioning, activation-region counts, and kernel-regression MSE are not magnitude-aware weight sharpness; Section 3.3 explicitly measures absolute generalization error rather than the training–test gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present trainability, expressivity, and generalization as distinct, complementary properties assessed through training-free indicators, and conclude that combining them improves NAS accuracy and efficiency. They also emphasize visualizing search trajectories to interpret architecture-space geometry.
record.recipe_differences: Training-free NTK and activation-pattern metrics evaluated over NAS architectures; no random-label fitting, width sweep, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal test.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlations are specific to NAS-Bench-201 on CIFAR-100; the authors state that the metrics have different correlations with training and test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On NAS-Bench-201 CIFAR-100, initialization-based NTK conditioning, activation-region counts, NTK regression MSE, and their combined rankings correlate with architecture training and test accuracy. Combined rankings yield correlations of −0.64 and −0.65, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-free architecture indicators can rank training and held-out accuracy across a fixed image-classification search space.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The reported accuracy correlations are on one search space and dataset in Figure 1, and do not establish a relation to the training–test gap or to trained-network sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results identified. Search-performance results compare NAS methods and do not test the listed generalization versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy compared with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned or imposed local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that recover performance.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness versus training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 confirms all eight extracted correlation values. The changed states indicate that these measures cannot establish any listed version, not that the reported correlations are absent. Architecture-space landscape visualizations likewise do not test V7's weight-perturbation claim.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error across network widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected network generalization.
Generalization differences between adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Effects of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.
